`reset` is still `reject`, the three blocks being held by the values 2, 3, 4 (§78.2); after their
end, `reset` and the reissue are `ok`. With the blocks issued into fields of the structure: the
expected verdicts (§78.2, §69 effect, §77). **MISMATCH** on the literal reading (after `endUse`
of the structure: expected `ok`, obtained `reject`); cause: case defect, the material does not say
which values hold the blocks. -/
theorem W3 : RunsTo K0 [] w3o w3 ∧ ResetD 0 w3 .reject ∧
    RunsTo K0 [] (w3o ++ [.endUse 5]) w3e ∧ ResetD 0 w3e .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] (w3o ++ [.endUse 5, .endUse 2, .endUse 3, .endUse 4, .reset 0, .issue 0 [10] 2]) ∧
    RunsTo K0 [] w3vo w3v ∧ ResetD 0 w3v .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] (w3vo ++ [.endUse 2, .reset 0, .issue 0 [10] 3]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), rejects (k := K0) (o := .reset 0) (by decide), runsTo (by decide),
    rejects (k := K0) (o := .reset 0) (by decide), runsTo (by decide), runsTo (by decide),
    rejects (k := K0) (o := .reset 0) (by decide), runsTo (by decide)⟩

end Ern.Corpus.MM3H

import Ern.MemoryModel.Machine

/-!
# Corpus MM2-H on the memory machine (test module, spec v0 Parts II–III, §8–§20)

Test module. It states no semantics: it runs the MM2-H corpus (non-normative validation
material, 17 identifiers, H13 split into H13a and H13b, 18 scenarios) on the relations of
`Ern.MemoryModel.Machine`.

Each case gives a state reached from the empty state, an admissible initial state (§9 ¶9), by an
execution of `ok` steps (`Exec`, §20.3 ¶3), and the outcome of the normative relation at that
state (`ReadStep`, `WriteStep`, `DeallocStep`, `AllocStep`, §20.1), proved by `decide` or by the
machine lemmas. Each `ub` case has a separate `_twin` theorem for the corpus's positive twin.
The docstring of each theorem states the expected verdict from the corpus, the obtained verdict,
and the class (rule "classement" of the corpus: `N2` = memory machine). Where the obtained
verdict differs from the expected one, the docstring says "Mismatch" and the case is kept as
written, not corrected.

Context of every execution (§20.3 ¶1, §20.3 ¶3: explicit context parameters): compatibility is
equality of the presented authority with the recorded token (§17 ¶4); read and write
obligations are the machine's explicit test instances `Witness.obR` and `Witness.obW` (both parts
`True`), except in H14, which needs a false static part.

Open obligations, not declared passed: H10 address formation (§14 ¶4, §19), H13a at language
level (§10 ¶4, §19), H13b (§19).
-/

namespace Ern.Corpus.MM2H

open Ern.MemoryModel.Machine

/-! ## Run builders -/

section Builders

variable {Ty : Type} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {R : ReadOblSpec Ty} {W : WriteOblSpec Ty}

/-- An execution extended by one `ok` step at its end is an execution (§20.1 ¶2, §20.3 ¶3). -/
theorem exec_snoc {ops : List (Op Ty)} {op : Op Ty} {s₀ s s' : State}
    (h : Exec C R W ops s₀ s) (hs : Step C R W op s s') : Exec C R W (ops ++ [op]) s₀ s' := by
  induction h with
  | nil => exact .cons hs (.nil _)
  | cons h₀ _ ih => exact .cons h₀ (ih hs)

/-- Appending an `ok` raw creation to an execution from the empty state. The decidable form
`AllocPreDec` suffices because every reached state satisfies freshness (§9 ¶7, §9 ¶9, §9 ¶11). -/
theorem run_alloc {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s : State} {space base size align : Nat}
    {freeAuth : Option Nat} (h : Exec C R W ops State.empty s)
    (hp : AllocPreDec s space base size align) :
    Exec C R W (ops ++ [.alloc space base size align freeAuth]) State.empty
      (s.alloc space base size align freeAuth) :=
  exec_snoc h (.alloc (.ok ((allocPreDec_iff (h.admissible admissible_empty).wf).1 hp)))

/-- Appending an `ok` raw write to an execution from the empty state (§16, §20.2 ¶2). -/
theorem run_write {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s : State} {ac : Access} {t : Ty}
    {w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} (h : Exec C R W ops State.empty s) (hc : CanWrite s ac)
    (hd : W.dec s ac t w) (hs : W.stat s ac t w) :
    Exec C R W (ops ++ [.write ac t w]) State.empty (s.write ac w) :=
  exec_snoc h (.write (.ok ⟨hc, hd, hs⟩))

/-- Appending an `ok` raw deallocation to an execution from the empty state (§17, §20.2 ¶2). -/
theorem run_dealloc {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s : State} {id auth : Nat}
    (h : Exec C R W ops State.empty s) (hc : CanDealloc C s id auth) :
    Exec C R W (ops ++ [.dealloc id auth]) State.empty (s.dealloc id) :=
  exec_snoc h (.dealloc (.ok hc))

/-- Appending an `ok` raw read to an execution from the empty state; the state is unchanged
(§15, §20.2 ¶1). -/
theorem run_read {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s : State} {ac : Access} {t : Ty} {v : List AByte}
    (h : Exec C R W ops State.empty s) (hr : ReadStep R ac t s (.ok v)) :
    Exec C R W (ops ++ [.read ac t]) State.empty s :=
  exec_snoc h (.read hr)

/-- At a state reached from the empty state, a creation whose decidable preconditions fail is
`ub` (§9 ¶11, §20.1 ¶2). -/
theorem allocStep_ub {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s : State} {space base size align : Nat}
    {freeAuth : Option Nat} (h : Exec C R W ops State.empty s)
    (hn : ¬ AllocPreDec s space base size align) :
    AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s .ub :=
  .ub (mt (allocPreDec_iff (h.admissible admissible_empty).wf).2 hn)

/-- At a state reached from the empty state, a creation whose decidable preconditions hold is
`ok` with the creation effect (§9 ¶11, §20.1 ¶2). -/
theorem allocStep_ok {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s : State} {space base size align : Nat}
    {freeAuth : Option Nat} (h : Exec C R W ops State.empty s)
    (hp : AllocPreDec s space base size align) :
    AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s (.ok (s.alloc space base size align freeAuth)) :=
  .ok ((allocPreDec_iff (h.admissible admissible_empty).wf).1 hp)

end Builders

/-! ## Context and common states -/

/-- Read obligations of the corpus context: the machine's explicit test instance, both parts
`True` (§20.3 ¶1). -/
abbrev ctxR : ReadOblSpec Unit := Witness.obR.toSpec

/-- Write obligations of the corpus context: the machine's explicit test instance, both parts
`True` (§20.3 ¶1). -/
abbrev ctxW : WriteOblSpec Unit := Witness.obW.toSpec

/-- Executions of the corpus context from the empty state (§9 ¶9, §20.3 ¶3): compatibility is
equality of presented authority and recorded token (§17 ¶2, §17 ¶4), obligations `ctxR`,
`ctxW`. -/
abbrev Run (ops : List (Op Unit)) (s : State) : Prop :=
  Exec (· = ·) ctxR ctxW ops State.empty s

/-- A read whose interpreter result is `o` has the relational outcome `o` (§20.3 ¶3, by
`read_sound`). -/
theorem readStep_of {ac : Access} {s : State} {o : ReadOutcome}
    (h : read Witness.obR ac () s trivial = o) : ReadStep ctxR ac () s o :=
  read_sound h

/-- Write access to `[96, 104)` with provenance `p` (§12 ¶1). -/
def wr (p : Nat) : Access := ⟨96, p, 8, .write⟩

/-- Read access to `[96, 104)` with provenance `p` (§12 ¶1). -/
def rd (p : Nat) : Access := ⟨96, p, 8, .read⟩

/-- One live allocation: identity `0`, space `0`, base `96`, size `8`, alignment `8`,
deallocation token `7` (§9 ¶1, §9 ¶11). -/
abbrev a8 : State := State.empty.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)

/-- `a8` after a write of `Witness.w₀` (value `i + 1`, no provenance) over its whole range
(§16 ¶2). -/
abbrev a8w : State := a8.write (wr 0) Witness.w₀

/-- `a8` after deallocation of allocation `0` (§17 ¶3). -/
abbrev a8d : State := a8.dealloc 0

/-- The empty state is reached by the empty execution (§9 ¶9). -/
theorem run_empty : Run [] State.empty :=
  .nil _

/-- `a8` is reached by one `ok` creation (§9 ¶11). -/
theorem run_a8 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 :=
  run_alloc (.nil _) (by decide)

/-- `a8w` is reached by a creation and an `ok` write (§9 ¶11, §16). -/
theorem run_a8w : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀] a8w :=
  run_write run_a8 (by decide) trivial trivial

/-- `a8d` is reached by a creation and an `ok` deallocation (§9 ¶11, §17). -/
theorem run_a8d : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .dealloc 0 7] a8d :=
  run_dealloc run_a8 (by decide)

/-! ## H01 — address reuse after deallocation -/

/-- State of H01: `a8w`, deallocation of `0`, then a new allocation at the same base `96`,
which receives identity `1` (§13 ¶1, §13 ¶2). -/
abbrev h01 : State := (a8w.dealloc 0).alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)

/-- Operations reaching `h01` (§9 ¶11, §16, §17). -/
abbrev h01Ops : List (Op Unit) :=
  [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀, .dealloc 0 7, .alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)]

/-- `h01` is reached, and the new allocation lies at the old base `96` (§13 ¶2). -/
theorem run_h01 : Run h01Ops h01 ∧ ∃ b, h01.allocs 1 = some b ∧ b.live = true ∧ b.base = 96 :=
  ⟨run_alloc (run_dealloc run_a8w (by decide)) (by decide), _, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩

/-- H01. Free, allocate at the same base, read through the old access. Expected `ub`;
obtained `ub`: the old provenance designates the dead allocation `0` (§12 ¶3, §13 ¶2, §15.1,
§17 ¶3). Class N2. -/
theorem H01 : Run h01Ops h01 ∧ ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () h01 .ub :=
  ⟨run_h01.1, readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-- H01 twin as written ("read through the new access"). Expected `ok`; obtained `ub`.
Mismatch, case defect: the new allocation is wholly uninitialized (§10 ¶5), so a read of
length `8` through it violates §15.3. Class N2. -/
theorem H01_twin : Run h01Ops h01 ∧ ReadStep ctxR (rd 1) () h01 .ub :=
  ⟨run_h01.1, readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-- Variant of the H01 twin, not the corpus's twin: a write through the new access before the
read. Obtained `ok` with the written bytes (§16 ¶2, §16 ¶5). It shows that the `ub` of
`H01_twin` comes from §10 ¶5, not from the address reuse. -/
theorem H01_twin_variant :
    Run (h01Ops ++ [.write (wr 1) () Witness.w₀]) (h01.write (wr 1) Witness.w₀) ∧
    ReadStep ctxR (rd 1) () (h01.write (wr 1) Witness.w₀) (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 8)) :=
  ⟨run_write run_h01.1 (by decide) trivial trivial, readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-! ## H02, H03 — deallocation -/

/-- H02. Double deallocation. Expected `ub`; obtained `ub`: the allocation is dead (§17.1,
§17 ¶3). Class N2. -/
theorem H02 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .dealloc 0 7] a8d ∧
    DeallocStep (· = ·) 0 7 a8d .ub :=
  ⟨run_a8d, .ub (by decide)⟩

/-- H02 twin: a single deallocation. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` (§17.1, §17.2). Class N2. -/
theorem H02_twin : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ DeallocStep (· = ·) 0 7 a8 (.ok a8d) :=
  ⟨run_a8, .ok (by decide)⟩

/-- H03. Deallocation with an authority (`8`) not compatible with the token (`7`) under the
context relation. Expected `ub`; obtained `ub` (§17.2, §17 ¶4, §20.3 ¶3). Class N2. -/
theorem H03 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ DeallocStep (· = ·) 0 8 a8 .ub :=
  ⟨run_a8, .ub (by decide)⟩

/-- H03 twin: compatible authority `7`. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` (§17.2). Class N2. -/
theorem H03_twin : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ DeallocStep (· = ·) 0 7 a8 (.ok a8d) :=
  H02_twin

H02_twin

/-! ## H04, H05, H06 — read conditions -/

/-- H04. Read of uninitialized bytes, right after creation. Expected `ub`; obtained `ub`
(§10 ¶5, §15.3). Class N2. -/
theorem H04 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () a8 .ub :=
  ⟨run_a8, readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-- H04 twin: write, then read. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` with the written bytes (§16 ¶2,
§16 ¶5). Class N2. -/
theorem H04_twin : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀] a8w ∧
    ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () a8w (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 8)) :=
  ⟨run_a8w, readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-- H05. Read of `[101, 105)`, one byte past the end `104`. Expected `ub`; obtained `ub`
(§15 ¶1, §15.2). Class N2. -/
theorem H05 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀] a8w ∧
    ReadStep ctxR ⟨101, 0, 4, .read⟩ () a8w .ub :=
  ⟨run_a8w, readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-- H05 twin: read of `[100, 104)`, ending at the end. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` with the
written bytes (§15 ¶1, §16 ¶5). Class N2. -/
theorem H05_twin : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀] a8w ∧
    ReadStep ctxR ⟨100, 0, 4, .read⟩ () a8w (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 4 4)) :=
  ⟨run_a8w, readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-- Zero-length read access at address `104`, just after the end of `[96, 104)` (§15 ¶3). -/
def rz : Access := ⟨104, 0, 0, .read⟩

/-- H06. Zero-length read just after the end of a dead allocation. Expected `ub`; obtained
`ub` (§15.1, §15 ¶3, §17 ¶3). Class N2. -/
theorem H06 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .dealloc 0 7] a8d ∧ ReadStep ctxR rz () a8d .ub :=
  ⟨run_a8d, readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-- H06 twin: same access, allocation live. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` with no bytes: the
spatial condition admits address `b + s` and no initialized byte is required (§15 ¶3).
Class N2. -/
theorem H06_twin : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ ReadStep ctxR rz () a8 (.ok []) :=
  ⟨run_a8, readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-! ## H07, H08 — creation preconditions -/

/-- H07. Creation of `[100, 108)` in space `0`, overlapping the live `[96, 104)` of the same
space. Expected `ub`; obtained `ub` (§9 ¶3, §9 ¶11). Class N2. -/
theorem H07 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ AllocStep 0 100 8 4 none a8 .ub :=
  ⟨run_a8, allocStep_ub run_a8 (by decide)⟩

/-- H07 twins: the same creation in another space (`1`), or in space `0` after the
overlapped allocation died. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` (§9 ¶3, §9 ¶11). Class N2. -/
theorem H07_twin : AllocStep 1 100 8 4 none a8 (.ok (a8.alloc 1 100 8 4 none)) ∧
    Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .dealloc 0 7] a8d ∧
    AllocStep 0 100 8 4 none a8d (.ok (a8d.alloc 0 100 8 4 none)) :=
  ⟨allocStep_ok run_a8 (by decide), run_a8d, allocStep_ok run_a8d (by decide)⟩

/-- H08. From the empty state (admissible, §9 ¶9): alignment `3`, not a power of two, with
base `96` a multiple of `3`; and base `100` not a multiple of alignment `8`. Expected `ub`;
obtained `ub` for both (§9 ¶4, §9 ¶11). Class N2. -/
theorem H08 : AllocStep 0 96 8 3 none State.empty .ub ∧ AllocStep 0 100 8 8 none State.empty .ub :=
  ⟨allocStep_ub run_empty (by decide), allocStep_ub run_empty (by decide)⟩

/-- H08 twins: valid alignment `4` for each faulty creation. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok`
(§9 ¶4, §9 ¶11). Class N2. -/
theorem H08_twin :
    AllocStep 0 96 8 4 none State.empty (.ok (State.empty.alloc 0 96 8 4 none)) ∧
    AllocStep 0 100 8 4 none State.empty (.ok (State.empty.alloc 0 100 8 4 none)) :=
  ⟨allocStep_ok run_empty (by decide), allocStep_ok run_empty (by decide)⟩

/-! ## H09, H10 — write authority, derivation -/

/-- H09. Write through an access whose elementary authority is `read`. Expected `ub`;
obtained `ub` (§12 ¶4, §16.3). Class N2. -/
theorem H09 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧
    WriteStep ctxW ⟨96, 0, 8, .read⟩ () Witness.w₀ a8 .ub :=
  ⟨run_a8, .ub fun h => absurd h.1 (by decide)⟩

/-- H09 twin: write authority. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` (§16.3). Class N2. -/
theorem H09_twin : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧
    WriteStep ctxW (wr 0) () Witness.w₀ a8 (.ok a8w) :=
  ⟨run_a8, .ok ⟨by decide, trivial, trivial⟩⟩

/-- Source access of H10: write access to `[96, 100)` of allocation `0` (§12 ¶1). -/
def h10src : Access := ⟨96, 0, 4, .write⟩

/-- Access formed outside the source range `[96, 100)` but inside the allocation:
`[100, 104)` (§14 ¶4). -/
def h10out : Access := ⟨100, 0, 4, .write⟩

/-- Access formed outside the source range and outside the allocation: `[104, 108)`
(§14 ¶4). -/
def h10past : Access := ⟨104, 0, 4, .write⟩

/-- Restrictive derivation of `h10src` inside its range: `[98, 100)` (§14 ¶1). -/
def h10in : Access := ⟨98, 0, 2, .write⟩

/-- H10, use of an access formed outside the source range that leaves the allocation.
Expected `ub` for the use; obtained `ub` (§15 ¶1, §16.2). The formation itself has no
transition in the machine and no verdict: open obligation (§14 ¶4, §19), not declared passed.
Class N2. -/
theorem H10 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ ¬ Derive h10src h10past ∧
    WriteStep ctxW h10past () Witness.w₀ a8 .ub :=
  ⟨run_a8, fun h => absurd h.2.1 (by decide), .ub fun h => absurd h.1 (by decide)⟩

/-- H10, use of an access formed outside the source range but inside the allocation.
Expected `ub`; obtained `ok`. Mismatch, case defect: provenance has allocation granularity in
the machine (§14 ¶2), so only leaving the allocation makes the use `ub` (§16.2); the scenario
does not say which. Class N2. -/
theorem H10_inside : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ ¬ Derive h10src h10out ∧
    WriteStep ctxW h10out () Witness.w₀ a8 (.ok (a8.write h10out Witness.w₀)) :=
  ⟨run_a8, fun h => absurd h.2.1 (by decide), .ok ⟨by decide, trivial, trivial⟩⟩

/-- H10 twin: a restrictive derivation inside the source range, then use. Expected `ok`;
obtained `ok` (§14 ¶1, §16). Class N2. -/
theorem H10_twin : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ Derive h10src h10in ∧
    WriteStep ctxW h10in () Witness.w₀ a8 (.ok (a8.write h10in Witness.w₀)) :=
  ⟨run_a8, ⟨by decide, by decide, rfl, by decide⟩, .ok ⟨by decide, trivial, trivial⟩⟩

/-! ## H11, H12 — read-after-write and non-interference -/

/-- H11. Write `[96, 104)`, read the contained subrange `[98, 101)`. Expected: the written
sub-contents; obtained `ok` with positions `2..4` of the written representation (§16 ¶5).
Class N2. -/
theorem H11 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀] a8w ∧
    ReadStep ctxR ⟨98, 0, 3, .read⟩ () a8w (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 2 3)) :=
  ⟨run_a8w, readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-- Second written representation of H12: byte `170`, no provenance, at every position
(§10 ¶2). -/
def w₁ : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat := fun _ => (170, none)

/-- State of H12: allocations `0` (`[96, 104)`) and `1` (`[128, 136)`, same space), and
`[96, 100)` written with `Witness.w₀` (§9 ¶3, §16 ¶2). -/
abbrev h12 : State := (a8.alloc 0 128 8 8 none).write ⟨96, 0, 4, .write⟩ Witness.w₀

/-- Operations reaching `h12` (§9 ¶11, §16). -/
abbrev h12Ops : List (Op Unit) :=
  [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .alloc 0 128 8 8 none, .write ⟨96, 0, 4, .write⟩ () Witness.w₀]

/-- `h12` is reached (§9 ¶11, §16). -/
theorem run_h12 : Run h12Ops h12 :=
  run_write (run_alloc run_a8 (by decide)) (by decide) trivial trivial

/-- H12. After `h12`, a write of a disjoint range of the same allocation (`[100, 104)`), or a
write of the other allocation, leaves the read of `[96, 100)` unchanged. Expected: contents
unchanged; obtained: the same `ok` bytes before and after each write (§16 ¶3, §16 ¶5).
Class N2. -/
theorem H12 : Run h12Ops h12 ∧
    ReadStep ctxR ⟨96, 0, 4, .read⟩ () h12 (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 4)) ∧
    Run (h12Ops ++ [.write ⟨100, 0, 4, .write⟩ () w₁]) (h12.write ⟨100, 0, 4, .write⟩ w₁) ∧
    ReadStep ctxR ⟨96, 0, 4, .read⟩ () (h12.write ⟨100, 0, 4, .write⟩ w₁)
      (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 4)) ∧
    Run (h12Ops ++ [.write ⟨128, 1, 8, .write⟩ () w₁]) (h12.write ⟨128, 1, 8, .write⟩ w₁) ∧
    ReadStep ctxR ⟨96, 0, 4, .read⟩ () (h12.write ⟨128, 1, 8, .write⟩ w₁)
      (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 4)) :=
  ⟨run_h12, readStep_of (by decide), run_write run_h12 (by decide) trivial trivial,
    readStep_of (by decide), run_write run_h12 (by decide) trivial trivial,
    readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-! ## H13a, H13b — pointer bytes -/

/-- Representation written as a pointer: byte values of the address `64` (low byte first) and
provenance `0`, the allocation at `64`, on every byte. The byte encoding is a choice of this
test; the provenance comes from the written representation (§10 ¶4, §16 ¶2). -/
def ptrRep : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat := fun i => (if i = 0 then 64 else 0, some 0)

/-- State of H13a before the copy: allocations `0` (`[64, 72)`), `1` (`[96, 104)`, source)
and `2` (`[128, 136)`, destination); `ptrRep` written over the source (§9 ¶11, §16 ¶2). -/
abbrev h13Src : State :=
  (((State.empty.alloc 0 64 8 8 none).alloc 0 96 8 8 none).alloc 0 128 8 8 none).write
    ⟨96, 1, 8, .write⟩ ptrRep

/-- Read access to source byte `k` (§12 ¶1). -/
def srcByte (k : Nat) : Access := ⟨96 + k, 1, 1, .read⟩

/-- Write access to destination byte `k` (§12 ¶1). -/
def dstByte (k : Nat) : Access := ⟨128 + k, 2, 1, .write⟩

/-- Representation supplied by the copy of byte `k`: the value and provenance of source byte
`k` (§16 ¶2). `cp_reads` shows that it is the abstract byte the copy read (§20.2 ¶1). -/
def copyRep (k : Nat) : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat := fun _ => ptrRep k

/-- State after copying the first `k` bytes, one byte per write (§16 ¶2). -/
def cp : Nat → State
  | 0 => h13Src
  | k + 1 => (cp k).write (dstByte k) (copyRep k)

/-- Operations reaching `cp k`: set-up, then for each byte a read of the source byte and a
write of the destination byte (§15, §16). -/
def cpOps : Nat → List (Op Unit)
  | 0 => [.alloc 0 64 8 8 none, .alloc 0 96 8 8 none, .alloc 0 128 8 8 none,
      .write ⟨96, 1, 8, .write⟩ () ptrRep]
  | k + 1 => cpOps k ++ [.read (srcByte k) ()] ++ [.write (dstByte k) () (copyRep k)]

/-- Before copying byte `k`, the read of source byte `k` is `ok` and returns exactly the value
and provenance that `copyRep k` supplies (§15, §16 ¶5, §20.2 ¶1). -/
theorem cp_reads : ∀ k, k < 8 →
    read Witness.obR (srcByte k) () (cp k) trivial = .ok [.init (ptrRep k).1 (ptrRep k).2] := by
  decide

/-- Before copying byte `k`, the write of destination byte `k` satisfies the kernel write
conditions (§16.1–§16.3). -/
theorem cp_writes : ∀ k, k < 8 → CanWrite (cp k) (dstByte k) := by
  decide

/-- The copy of the first `k ≤ 8` bytes is an execution of `ok` steps from the empty state
(§20.3 ¶3). -/
theorem run_cp : ∀ k, k ≤ 8 → Run (cpOps k) (cp k)
  | 0, _ =>
    run_write (run_alloc (run_alloc (run_alloc (.nil _) (by decide)) (by decide)) (by decide))
      (by decide) trivial trivial
  | k + 1, hk =>
    run_write (run_read (run_cp k (Nat.le_of_succ_le hk)) (read_sound (cp_reads k hk)))
      (cp_writes k hk) trivial trivial

/-- The eight abstract bytes of `ptrRep`, each with provenance `0` (§10 ¶2). -/
def ptrBytes : List AByte :=
  [.init 64 (some 0), .init 0 (some 0), .init 0 (some 0), .init 0 (some 0),
    .init 0 (some 0), .init 0 (some 0), .init 0 (some 0), .init 0 (some 0)]

/-- H13a. Pointer bytes copied byte by byte, each write supplying the abstract byte just read.
Expected: the provenance of each byte is kept. Obtained, at relation level: every copy read is
`ok` with the byte's value and provenance, and after the copy the destination reads exactly
the source bytes, provenance `0` on each (§16 ¶2, §16 ¶5, §20.2 ¶1). Open obligation, not
declared passed: whether a byte copy of the language supplies the read provenance is not fixed
(§10 ¶4, §19 ¶3). Class N2. -/
theorem H13a : Run (cpOps 8) (cp 8) ∧
    (∀ k, k < 8 → ReadStep ctxR (srcByte k) () (cp k) (.ok [.init (ptrRep k).1 (ptrRep k).2])) ∧
    ReadStep ctxR ⟨128, 2, 8, .read⟩ () (cp 8) (.ok ptrBytes) ∧
    ReadStep ctxR ⟨96, 1, 8, .read⟩ () (cp 8) (.ok ptrBytes) :=
  ⟨run_cp 8 (Nat.le_refl _), fun k hk => read_sound (cp_reads k hk),
    readStep_of (by decide +kernel), readStep_of (by decide +kernel)⟩

/-- H13b. Rebuilding a usable access from the copied bytes or from the integer `64`.
Expected: to be arbitrated. Obtained: no verdict; the machine has no conversion from an integer
or from bytes to an access, and an access to address `64` gets `ok` or `ub` according to the
provenance a conversion rule would give it: `0` (the provenance stored in the copied bytes)
gives `ok`, `2` (the allocation holding the copied bytes) gives `ub`. Open obligation, not
declared passed (§19.2, §19.3, §19 ¶3). Class N2. -/
theorem H13b_open :
    WriteStep ctxW ⟨64, 0, 1, .write⟩ () w₁ (cp 8) (.ok ((cp 8).write ⟨64, 0, 1, .write⟩ w₁)) ∧
    WriteStep ctxW ⟨64, 2, 1, .write⟩ () w₁ (cp 8) .ub :=
  ⟨.ok ⟨by decide, trivial, trivial⟩, .ub fun h => absurd h.1 (by decide)⟩

/-! ## H14 — false static obligation -/

/-- Read obligations whose decidable part is `True` and whose static part is `P` at every read
(§20.3 ¶1, §20.3 ¶2): an explicit context with a false (`P = False`) or true (`P = True`)
static obligation. -/
def obStat (P : Prop) : ReadObl Unit :=
  { dec := fun _ _ _ => True, stat := fun _ _ _ => P, decInst := fun _ _ _ => instDecidableTrue }

/-- H14. Read of initialized bytes satisfying every kernel condition, under a context whose
static obligation is false. Expected: relation `ub`, interpreter not callable. Obtained: the
relation is `ub` (§20.1 ¶2, "including when the obligation is static"), and no proof of the
static part exists, so `read (obStat False) (rd 0) () a8w` cannot be applied (§20.3 ¶3).
Class N2. -/
theorem H14 :
    Exec (· = ·) (obStat False).toSpec ctxW [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀]
      State.empty a8w ∧
    CanRead a8w (rd 0) ∧ ReadStep (obStat False).toSpec (rd 0) () a8w .ub ∧
    ¬ (obStat False).stat a8w (rd 0) () :=
  ⟨run_write (run_alloc (.nil _) (by decide)) (by decide) trivial trivial, by decide,
    .ub fun h => h.2.2, id⟩

/-- H14 twin: same access, static obligation true. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` by the
relation and by the interpreter, with the same bytes (§20.1 ¶2, §20.3 ¶3). Class N2. -/
theorem H14_twin :
    Exec (· = ·) (obStat True).toSpec ctxW [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀]
      State.empty a8w ∧
    ReadStep (obStat True).toSpec (rd 0) () a8w (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 8)) ∧
    read (obStat True) (rd 0) () a8w trivial = .ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 8) :=
  have hr : read (obStat True) (rd 0) () a8w trivial = .ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 8) := by
    decide
  ⟨run_write (run_alloc (.nil _) (by decide)) (by decide) trivial trivial, read_sound hr, hr⟩

/-! ## H15, H16 — zero-size allocations, deallocation with a live access -/

/-- State of H15: two allocations of size `0` at base `96` in space `0` (§9 ¶3). -/
abbrev h15 : State := (State.empty.alloc 0 96 0 8 none).alloc 0 96 0 8 none

/-- H15. Two zero-size allocations live at the same base. Expected `ok`, distinct identities;
obtained: both creations `ok`, the state is admissible, identities `0` and `1` are both live
at base `96` with size `0` (§9 ¶3, §9 ¶8, §13 ¶1). Class N2. -/
theorem H15 : Run [.alloc 0 96 0 8 none, .alloc 0 96 0 8 none] h15 ∧ Admissible h15 ∧
    (∃ a, h15.allocs 0 = some a ∧ a.live = true ∧ a.base = 96 ∧ a.size = 0) ∧
    (∃ b, h15.allocs 1 = some b ∧ b.live = true ∧ b.base = 96 ∧ b.size = 0) :=
  have hr : Run [.alloc 0 96 0 8 none, .alloc 0 96 0 8 none] h15 :=
    run_alloc (run_alloc (.nil _) (by decide)) (by decide)
  ⟨hr, hr.admissible admissible_empty, ⟨_, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩, ⟨_, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩⟩

/-- State of H16: `a8w` (written through `wr 0`), then deallocation of `0` (§17 ¶3). -/
abbrev h16 : State := a8w.dealloc 0

/-- H16. Deallocation while the access `wr 0` designates the allocation, then use of that
access. Expected `ok`, then `ub`; obtained: the deallocation is `ok` (its conditions do not
mention existing accesses, §17.1, §17.2), then the write and the read through provenance `0`
are `ub` (§15.1, §16.1, §17 ¶3). Prevention belongs to the access discipline. Class N2. -/
theorem H16 :
    Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀, .dealloc 0 7] h16 ∧
    DeallocStep (· = ·) 0 7 a8w (.ok h16) ∧
    WriteStep ctxW (wr 0) () Witness.w₀ h16 .ub ∧ ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () h16 .ub :=
  ⟨run_dealloc run_a8w (by decide), .ok (by decide), .ub fun h => absurd h.1 (by decide),
    readStep_of (by decide)⟩

/-! ## H17 — relation and interpreter -/

/-- On a state, every outcome of the read relation is the interpreter's result and conversely
(§20.3 ¶3, `read_sound`, `read_complete`). -/
theorem read_agree (ac : Access) (s : State) (o : ReadOutcome) :
    ReadStep ctxR ac () s o ↔ read Witness.obR ac () s trivial = o :=
  ⟨fun h => read_complete h trivial, read_sound⟩

/-- H17. Read by the relation and by the interpreter on admissible reached states. Expected:
same outcome, same value. Obtained: on `a8w` both give `ok` with the written bytes, on `a8`
both give `ub`, and the outcome sets coincide (§9 ¶8, §20.1, §20.2 ¶1, §20.3 ¶3). Class N2. -/
theorem H17 :
    Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀] a8w ∧ Admissible a8w ∧
    (∀ o, ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () a8w o ↔ read Witness.obR (rd 0) () a8w trivial = o) ∧
    ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () a8w (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 8)) ∧
    read Witness.obR (rd 0) () a8w trivial = .ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 8) ∧
    Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ Admissible a8 ∧
    (∀ o, ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () a8 o ↔ read Witness.obR (rd 0) () a8 trivial = o) ∧
    ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () a8 .ub ∧ read Witness.obR (rd 0) () a8 trivial = .ub :=
  ⟨run_a8w, run_a8w.admissible admissible_empty, read_agree _ _, H04_twin.2, by decide,
    run_a8, run_a8.admissible admissible_empty, read_agree _ _, H04.2, by decide⟩

## 14. Restrictive Derivation of Means of Access

A **restrictive derivation** of a means of access:

- preserves the source allocation's provenance;
- designates a **subrange** of the source access;
- confers no authority greater than that permitted by the source.

In the elementary memory machine, provenance has **allocation granularity**, not field or subrange granularity. Finer-grained rights restrictions are determined by the authority discipline defined in Part IV and following.

A valid restrictive derivation is not necessarily the only way to form an address or create a means of access. A safe abstraction may, through mechanisms and invariants yet to be defined, provide new rights to disjoint places; **the creation of rights is not reducible to restrictive derivation**.

Forming an address or a means of access is distinct from **using** it. Merely forming an out-of-bounds address is not automatically classified as UB; precise formation and conversion restrictions remain open in Section 19.

## 36. Shared Mutation and Internal Administration

An abstraction may keep its metadata in `SharedMutable` storage and modify it through `writeShared` to the extent permitted by the applicable rights and contracts. **Shared mutation of metadata does not, however, grant the right to create, recycle, or terminate exclusive authority over the administered storage.** Such operations require `internal` to be exercisable in `Modify` mode from the value administering the storage.

For every administrative abstraction, including arenas, `HandlePool`, and `DataStack`, **`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on the administering value**. The `writeShared` branch alone is insufficient. Operations issuing, recycling, ending, or invalidating regions must preserve active authorities and dependencies. Allocation through administration shared among simultaneous holders, under an interface not providing such exclusive exercise, cannot be expressed in safe code with only these sequential operations: any synchronized implementation of it belongs to Spec 2. These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel.

## 45. Parameters, Returns, and Reanchoring

A call parameter is an **active derived authority held by the caller** before being passed to the callee; its original provenance may go back to an earlier frame. This interpretation does not require that the authority was originally derived in the calling frame; that additional requirement belongs to Spec 3. The caller **yields** the authority to the new frame: it does not simultaneously retain a copy. If the authority remains in that frame upon return, `exitFrame` releases it; **it is not automatically returned to the caller**. To retain its own right, the caller may pass a **fresh derivative** of the authority it wishes to keep: this is ordinary reborrowing. The definition of ergonomic calling conventions is deferred to Spec 3.

A result is returned by a legal `transfer` into the result place provided by the caller as a `Modify` parameter. Surviving authorities and their dependencies are reanchored by `exitFrame` to still-valid origins. There is no standalone correspondence `M` and no implicit escape permission.

## 46. Arenas as Library Administration States

Each entry belongs to the library's abstract state, **separate from kernel state `S₃`**. It has the following fields:

```text
ArenaEntry {
    storage: PlaceId
    internal: AuthorityId
    available: Set<Leaf>
    issued: Set<(Region, AuthorityId)>
}
```

A region is **available if and only if each of its leaves belongs to `available`**; the empty region is always available. Issuance removes the leaves of the issued region from `available`. Reset restores all leaves of the administered storage to that set. The registry and its updates belong to the abstraction contract and create no kernel permissions.

The arena is **live** if `internal` is active. The **arena value** is the place holding `internal`, distinct from the possible owner of `storage`. Administered storage may be local, static, allocated, or issued by another arena, under `newArena` preconditions and applicable invariants. `available` and `issued` remain **in the library's arena entry**.

## 47. Initial State

The kernel's initial state contains only base frame 0 and the declared static storage. Every static leaf has its declared initial state, `Init` or `Uninit`. The roots of static places directly owned by frame 0 have a root `Modify` authority held by that frame; a static may also be owned by another static, in which case its root authority is held by the latter. The initial state invents no dynamic allocation, derived authority, or implicit anchor. The initial arena registry belongs to library state and is empty. The initial frame does not exit.

## 48. External Parametric Contract
## 81. Boundaries Remaining to Be Specified

This specification **does not by itself determine**: concurrency and synchronization effects (Spec 2); control-flow analysis, `defer`, and by-value calling conventions (Spec 3); representation criteria and typed formation of accesses (Spec 4); representation of library metadata, address width, encodings, and alignment/ABI obligations (Spec 11); or final translation of `noalias` properties (Spec 13). Leaving a rule open does not authorize a safe interface to cause UB; the implementation must fulfill or reject the obligations before exposing the operation to safe code.

/-!
# Combined library runner (test module)

A computable executor for the library corpus cases of
`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md`, over one combined library state: the kernel state
`S₃` shared by the arena registry of `Ern.MemoryModel.Arena` (Part XIV, §46), the pool registry of
`Ern.Lib.HandlePool` (contract "HandlePool v0.4 annex", non-normative) and the stack registry of
`Ern.Lib.DataStack` (contract "DS-v1", non-normative), with the fresh pool identity, the ghost
resolutions and the fresh mark identifier of those modules (§38: administrative states of library
abstractions are separate from `S₃`). This module is a test module: no model or library module
imports it.

* `COp`: the kernel operations O1–O16 (§60–§75), the arena operations O17–O19 (§76–§78), the pool
  operations and the stack operations, with their arguments.
* `CRel k C o`: the relation of `o`, read on the projection of `C` it acts on (`toL`, `toP`, `toD`):
  the relation of `Ern.Corpus.OpRel` for O1–O16, `issue`, `reset`; `NewArenaStep`, `NewPoolStep`,
  `NewStackStep` with the internals of all other live registries as their guard parameter (§56,
  §76.4); the pool and stack relations of the library modules.
* `cstep k C o`: the computed outcome (§58); `cstep_sound`: it is an outcome of `CRel`, `ok`,
  `reject` and `fail` alike.
* `crun`, `cfinal`, `CRunsTo`: a run from `CState.init statics` (§47) whose steps are all `ok`
  reaches a library-reachable state (`CReach`) whose kernel state is reached by kernel steps O1–O16
  and ends of slot contents (`HandlePool.XReach`): `freeSlot` is not a kernel `endUse`
  (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3), and `allocSlot` is a kernel `write` (§67) when some authority can
  write its destination, which `crun` checks. `CRunsTo.reachable`: a run without `freeSlot` ends
  in a state kernel-`Reachable` (§57).
-/

namespace Ern.Corpus.LibRunner

open Ern.MemoryModel Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.MemoryModel.Arena Ern.Corpus Ern.Lib

/-! ## Combined library state (§38, §46, §47, §56) -/

/-- The combined library state (§38, §46): the kernel state `S₃`, the arena registry (§46), the
pool registry, the next fresh pool identity and the ghost resolutions (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1,
D.2), the stack registry and the next fresh mark identifier (DS-v1). -/
structure CState where
  kern : S3
  arenas : List ArenaEntry
  pools : List HandlePool.Pool
  nId : Nat
  res : List HandlePool.Res
  stacks : List DataStack.Stack
  fresh : Nat

/-- Initial combined state (§47): the initial kernel state and empty registries. -/
def CState.init (statics : Statics) : CState := ⟨S3.init statics, [], [], 0, [], [], 0⟩

/-- The arena library state of `C` (§46). -/
def CState.toL (C : CState) : LState := ⟨C.kern, C.arenas⟩

/-- The pool library state of `C` (§38; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1). -/
def CState.toP (C : CState) : HandlePool.PState := ⟨C.kern, C.pools, C.nId, C.res⟩

/-- The stack library state of `C` (§38; DS-v1). -/
def CState.toD (C : CState) : DataStack.DState := ⟨C.kern, C.stacks, C.fresh⟩

/-- `C` with its kernel state and arena registry replaced (§46). -/
def CState.setL (C : CState) (L : LState) : CState := { C with kern := L.kern, arenas := L.arenas }

/-- `C` with its kernel state and pool library state replaced (§38; HandlePool v0.4 annex). -/
def CState.setP (C : CState) (P : HandlePool.PState) : CState :=
  { C with kern := P.kern, pools := P.pools, nId := P.nId, res := P.res }

/-- `C` with its kernel state and stack library state replaced (§38; DS-v1). -/
def CState.setD (C : CState) (D : DataStack.DState) : CState :=
  { C with kern := D.kern, stacks := D.stacks, fresh := D.fresh }

/-- The registries of live administrations other than the arena registry (§56, §76.4): the live
pools (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1) and the live stacks (DS-v1). -/
def CState.othersA (C : CState) : List (List Nat) :=
  [HandlePool.liveInternals C.kern C.pools, DataStack.stackInternals C.kern C.stacks]

/-- The registries of live administrations other than the pool registry (§56; HandlePool v0.4
annex, D.1): the live arenas (§46) and the live stacks (DS-v1). -/
def CState.othersP (C : CState) : List (List Nat) :=
  [Arena.liveInternals C.kern C.arenas, DataStack.stackInternals C.kern C.stacks]

/-- The registries of live administrations other than the stack registry (§56; DS-v1): the live
arenas (§46) and the live pools (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1). -/
def CState.othersD (C : CState) : List (List Nat) :=
  [Arena.liveInternals C.kern C.arenas, HandlePool.liveInternals C.kern C.pools]

/-! ## Operations and their relations (§58, §60–§78; HandlePool v0.4 annex; DS-v1) -/

/-- An operation of a library run: the kernel operations O1–O16 (§60–§75), the arena operations
O17–O19 (§76–§78), the pool operations (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1–D.3; pools and slots named by
their registry index) and the stack operations (DS-v1; stacks named by their registry index). -/
inductive COp where
  | derive (src : Nat) (region : List Nat) (m : Mode)
  | split (src : Nat) (rs : List (List Nat))
  | release (a : Nat)
  | transfer (src dst : Nat)
  | depend (q x : Nat)
  | enter (ps : List Nat) (ls : LocalShape)
  | exit
  | read (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat)
  | write (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat)
  | writeShared (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat)
  | pin (p : Nat)
  | unpin (p : Nat)
  | endUse (p : Nat)
  | free (p auth : Nat)
  | alloc (provider owner : Nat) (ls : LocalShape)
  | store (a p : Nat)
  | newArena (storage internal : Nat)
  | issue (i : Nat) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat)
  | reset (i : Nat)
  | newPool (storage internal : Nat)
  | allocSlot (j dst : Nat)
  | resolve (j : Nat) (h : HandlePool.Handle) (m : Mode)
  | resolveMany (j : Nat) (hs : List HandlePool.Handle) (m : Mode)
  | unresolve (c : Nat)
  | freeSlot (j : Nat) (h : HandlePool.Handle)
  | newStack (storage internal : Nat)
  | push (j size dst : Nat)
  | mark (j : Nat)
  | rewind (j : Nat) (m : DataStack.Mark)
  | grow (j b extra : Nat)

/-- An outcome of a projected library state read on the combined state (§58): `ok` through the
embedding `emb`, `reject` and `fail` unchanged. -/
def liftO {σ : Type} (emb : σ → CState) : Outcome3 σ → Outcome3 CState
  | .ok x => .ok (emb x)
  | .reject => .reject
  | .fail => .fail

/-- A relation on a projected library state read on combined outcomes (§58): `ok C'` when `C'` is
the embedding of an `ok` state of the relation; `reject`, `fail` as the relation. -/
def LiftR {σ : Type} (R : Outcome3 σ → Prop) (emb : σ → CState) : Outcome3 CState → Prop
  | .ok C' => ∃ x, R (.ok x) ∧ C' = emb x
  | .reject => R .reject
  | .fail => R .fail

/-- The relation of `o` from `C` (§58, §60–§78; HandlePool v0.4 annex; DS-v1), on the projection
it acts on: `OpRel` of `Ern.Corpus` for O1–O16, `issue` and `reset`; `newArena`, `newPool`,
`newStack` with the internals of every other live registry as their guard parameter (§56,
§76.4); the relations of the pool and stack modules. -/
def CRel (k : K) (C : CState) : COp → Outcome3 CState → Prop
  | .derive a r m => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.derive a r m)) C.setL
  | .split a rs => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.split a rs)) C.setL
  | .release a => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.release a)) C.setL
  | .transfer a b => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.transfer a b)) C.setL
  | .depend q x => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.depend q x)) C.setL
  | .enter ps ls => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.enter ps ls)) C.setL
  | .exit => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL .exit) C.setL
  | .read a ls => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.read a ls)) C.setL
  | .write a ls => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.write a ls)) C.setL
  | .writeShared a ls => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.writeShared a ls)) C.setL
  | .pin p => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.pin p)) C.setL
  | .unpin p => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.unpin p)) C.setL
  | .endUse p => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.endUse p)) C.setL
  | .free p a => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.free p a)) C.setL
  | .alloc pr ow ls => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.alloc pr ow ls)) C.setL
  | .store a p => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.store a p)) C.setL
  | .newArena st i => LiftR (NewArenaStep C.othersA st i C.toL) C.setL
  | .issue i r d => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.issue i r d)) C.setL
  | .reset i => LiftR (OpRel k C.toL (.reset i)) C.setL
  | .newPool st i => LiftR (HandlePool.NewPoolStep C.othersP st i C.toP) C.setP
  | .allocSlot j d => LiftR (HandlePool.AllocSlotStep j d C.toP) C.setP
  | .resolve j h m => LiftR (HandlePool.ResolveStep j h m C.toP) C.setP
  | .resolveMany j hs m => LiftR (HandlePool.ResolveManyStep k j hs m C.toP) C.setP
  | .unresolve c => LiftR (HandlePool.UnresolveStep c C.toP) C.setP
  | .freeSlot j h => LiftR (HandlePool.FreeSlotStep k j h C.toP) C.setP
  | .newStack st i => LiftR (DataStack.NewStackStep C.othersD st i C.toD) C.setD
  | .push j n d => LiftR (DataStack.PushStep k j n d C.toD) C.setD
  | .mark j => LiftR (DataStack.MarkStep j C.toD) C.setD
  | .rewind j m => LiftR (DataStack.RewindStep k j m C.toD) C.setD
  | .grow j b e => LiftR (DataStack.GrowStep k j b e C.toD) C.setD

/-- The operations that are not kernel steps O1–O16 nor sequences of them: `freeSlot` ends a slot
content under `ContentEndPre` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §69 effect). -/
def COp.kernelOnly : COp → Bool
  | .freeSlot .. => false
  | _ => true

/-! ## Executor -/

/-- The first free slot of a slot list and its index (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "`ok` choisit un
slot libre"; the lowest index is chosen, one of the outcomes the relation allows). -/
def firstFree : List HandlePool.Slot → Option (Nat × HandlePool.Slot)
  | [] => none
  | sl :: l => if sl.live then (firstFree l).map fun p => (p.1 + 1, p.2) else some (0, sl)

/-- An authority that can write the leaf `dst` (§67), searched among the authorities of `s`. -/
def writer (s : S3) (dst : Nat) : Option Nat :=
  (List.range s.A.length).find? fun a => decide (Write3Pre s a [dst])

/-- The kernel-side check of a step of `crun` (§67; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3): the handle write
of `allocSlot` is a kernel `write` by some authority. -/
def COp.kok (C : CState) : COp → Bool
  | .allocSlot _ dst => (writer C.kern dst).isSome
  | _ => true

section Exec

section Exec
variable (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable]
  [DecidablePred k.Pinned] [DecidablePred k.ExternalDone] [DecidablePred k.Deallocable]
  [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)] [∀ p ls s, Decidable (k.Satisfiable p ls s)]

/-- Computed outcome of `allocSlot(pool j, dst)` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §58). -/
def allocSlotOut (P : HandlePool.PState) (j dst : Nat) : Outcome3 HandlePool.PState :=
  match P.pools[j]? with
  | none => .reject
  | some pl =>
    if HandlePool.AllocSlotStatic P.kern pl dst then
      match firstFree pl.slots with
      | some (i, sl) => .ok (HandlePool.allocSlotEff P j pl i sl dst)
      | none => .fail
    else .reject

/-- Computed outcome of `resolve(h, m)` on pool `j` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §58). -/
def resolveOut (P : HandlePool.PState) (j : Nat) (h : HandlePool.Handle) (m : Mode) :
    Outcome3 HandlePool.PState :=
  match P.pools[j]? with
  | none => .reject
  | some pl =>
    if HandlePool.ResolveRight P.kern pl m then
      if HandlePool.HandleOK pl h then
        match pl.slots[h.slot]? with
        | some sl =>
          if DerivePre (HandlePool.compS P.kern pl m) P.kern.A.length
              (footprint P.kern.P sl.place) m then
            .ok { P with
              kern := deriveEff (HandlePool.compS P.kern pl m) P.kern.A.length
                (footprint P.kern.P sl.place) m
              res := P.res ++ [⟨pl.id, pl.internal, P.kern.A.length, m,
                [(P.kern.A.length + 1, h.slot, h.gen)]⟩] }
          else .reject
        | none => .reject
      else .fail
    else .reject

/-- Computed outcome of `resolveMany(hs, m)` on pool `j` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §58). -/
def resolveManyOut (P : HandlePool.PState) (j : Nat) (hs : List HandlePool.Handle) (m : Mode) :
    Outcome3 HandlePool.PState :=
  match P.pools[j]? with
  | none => .reject
  | some pl =>
    if HandlePool.ResolveRight P.kern pl m then
      if HandlePool.BatchOK pl hs m then
        if HandlePool.EntriesPre k m (HandlePool.compS P.kern pl m) P.kern.A.length
            (HandlePool.entryRegions P.kern pl hs) then
          .ok { P with
            kern := HandlePool.entriesEff m (HandlePool.compS P.kern pl m) P.kern.A.length
              (HandlePool.entryRegions P.kern pl hs)
            res := P.res ++ [⟨pl.id, pl.internal, P.kern.A.length, m,
              HandlePool.batchEntries P.kern.A.length hs⟩] }
        else .reject
      else .fail
    else .reject

/-- Computed outcome of `unresolve(c)` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §58). -/
def unresolveOut (P : HandlePool.PState) (c : Nat) : Outcome3 HandlePool.PState :=
  match HandlePool.findRes P c with
  | none => .reject
  | some r =>
    match HandlePool.releaseAll P.kern (HandlePool.unresolveList P.kern r) with
    | none => .reject
    | some s' => .ok { P with kern := s' }

/-- Computed outcome of `freeSlot(h)` on pool `j` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §58). -/
def freeSlotOut (P : HandlePool.PState) (j : Nat) (h : HandlePool.Handle) :
    Outcome3 HandlePool.PState :=
  match P.pools[j]? with
  | none => .reject
  | some pl =>
    if HandlePool.AdminRight P.kern pl then
      if HandlePool.HandleOK pl h then
        match pl.slots[h.slot]? with
        | some sl =>
          if HandlePool.ContentEndPre k P.kern sl.place pl.internal then
            .ok (HandlePool.freeSlotEff P j pl h.slot sl)
          else .reject
        | none => .reject
      else .fail
    else .reject

/-- Computed outcome of `push(j, size, dst)` (DS-v1; Part XIV, §77; §58). -/
def pushOut (D : DataStack.DState) (j size dst : Nat) : Outcome3 DataStack.DState :=
  match D.stacks[j]? with
  | none => .reject
  | some st =>
    if IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (DataStack.cellsOf st st.top size) dst then
      if st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length then
        if SplitPre k D.kern st.internal [DataStack.cellsOf st st.top size] then
          if StorePre (splitEff D.kern st.internal [DataStack.cellsOf st st.top size])
              D.kern.A.length dst then
            .ok ⟨storeEff (splitEff D.kern st.internal [DataStack.cellsOf st st.top size])
              D.kern.A.length dst,
              D.stacks.set j (DataStack.pushMeta st size D.kern.A.length dst), D.fresh⟩
          else .reject
        else .reject
      else .fail
    else .reject

/-- Computed outcome of `mark(j)` (DS-v1; §58). -/
def markOut (D : DataStack.DState) (j : Nat) : Outcome3 DataStack.DState :=
  match D.stacks[j]? with
  | none => .reject
  | some st => .ok ⟨D.kern, D.stacks.set j (DataStack.markMeta j st D.fresh), D.fresh + 1⟩

/-- Computed outcome of `rewind(j, m)` (DS-v1; Part XIV, §78; §58). -/
def rewindOut (D : DataStack.DState) (j : Nat) (m : DataStack.Mark) :
    Outcome3 DataStack.DState :=
  match D.stacks[j]? with
  | none => .reject
  | some st =>
    if DataStack.LiveMark j st m then
      if DataStack.AdminRight D.kern st then
        if SplitPre k D.kern st.internal [DataStack.above st m] then
          if ReleasePre (splitEff D.kern st.internal [DataStack.above st m])
              D.kern.A.length then
            .ok ⟨releaseEff (splitEff D.kern st.internal [DataStack.above st m])
              D.kern.A.length, D.stacks.set j (DataStack.rewindMeta st m), D.fresh⟩
          else .reject
        else .reject
      else .reject
    else .fail

/-- Computed outcome of `grow(j, b, extra)` (DS-v1; Part XIV, §77; §58). -/
def growOut (D : DataStack.DState) (j b extra : Nat) : Outcome3 DataStack.DState :=
  match D.stacks[j]? with
  | none => .reject
  | some st =>
    match st.block b with
    | none => .reject
    | some x =>
      if extra = 0 then .reject else
      if ReleasePre D.kern b then
        if IssueStatic (releaseEff D.kern b) st.entry
            (DataStack.cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst then
          if DataStack.InPlace st x extra then
            if SplitPre k (releaseEff D.kern b) st.internal
                [DataStack.cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)] then
              if StorePre (splitEff (releaseEff D.kern b) st.internal
                  [DataStack.cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)])
                  (releaseEff D.kern b).A.length x.dst then
                .ok ⟨storeEff (splitEff (releaseEff D.kern b) st.internal
                    [DataStack.cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)])
                    (releaseEff D.kern b).A.length x.dst,
                  D.stacks.set j (DataStack.growMeta st x extra (releaseEff D.kern b).A.length),
                  D.fresh⟩
              else .reject
            else .reject
          else .fail
        else .reject
      else .reject

/-- The computed outcome of `o` from `C` (§58, §60–§78; HandlePool v0.4 annex; DS-v1): the
executor of `Ern.Corpus` on the arena projection for O1–O16, `issue` and `reset`; the guard of §56
over all registries for the creation operations; the pool and stack executors above. -/
def cstep (C : CState) : COp → Outcome3 CState
  | .derive a r m => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.derive a r m))
  | .split a rs => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.split a rs))
  | .release a => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.release a))
  | .transfer a b => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.transfer a b))
  | .depend q x => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.depend q x))
  | .enter ps ls => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.enter ps ls))
  | .exit => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL .exit)
  | .read a ls => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.read a ls))
  | .write a ls => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.write a ls))
  | .writeShared a ls => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.writeShared a ls))
  | .pin p => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.pin p))
  | .unpin p => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.unpin p))
  | .endUse p => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.endUse p))
  | .free p a => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.free p a))
  | .alloc pr ow ls => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.alloc pr ow ls))
  | .store a p => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.store a p))
  | .newArena st i =>
    if NewArenaPre C.kern C.arenas C.othersA st i then .ok (C.setL (newArenaEff C.toL st i))
    else .reject
  | .issue i r d => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.issue i r d))
  | .reset i => liftO C.setL (lstep k C.toL (.reset i))
  | .newPool st i =>
    if HandlePool.NewPoolPre C.kern C.pools C.othersP st i then
      .ok (C.setP (HandlePool.newPoolEff C.toP st i))
    else .reject
  | .allocSlot j d => liftO C.setP (allocSlotOut C.toP j d)
  | .resolve j h m => liftO C.setP (resolveOut C.toP j h m)
  | .resolveMany j hs m => liftO C.setP (resolveManyOut k C.toP j hs m)
  | .unresolve c => liftO C.setP (unresolveOut C.toP c)
  | .freeSlot j h => liftO C.setP (freeSlotOut k C.toP j h)
  | .newStack st i =>
    if DataStack.NewStackPre C.kern C.stacks C.othersD st i then
      .ok (C.setD (DataStack.newStackEff C.toD st i))
    else .reject
  | .push j n d => liftO C.setD (pushOut k C.toD j n d)
  | .mark j => liftO C.setD (markOut C.toD j)
  | .rewind j m => liftO C.setD (rewindOut k C.toD j m)
  | .grow j b e => liftO C.setD (growOut k C.toD j b e)

/-- The state after `o` from `C` when it is `ok`; `C` otherwise (§58). -/
def cnext (C : CState) (o : COp) : CState :=
  match cstep k C o with
  | .ok C' => C'
  | _ => C

/-- The state reached by `os` from `C` when every step is `ok` and every `allocSlot` handle write
is a kernel write (§58, §67); `none` otherwise. -/
def crun (C : CState) : List COp → Option CState
  | [] => some C
  | o :: os =>
    match cstep k C o with
    | .ok C' => if o.kok C then crun C' os else none
    | _ => none

/-- The state reached by `os` from `CState.init statics` (§47); `CState.init statics` when the run
does not complete (used only under `(crun …).isSome = true`, see `crunsTo`). -/
def cfinal (statics : Statics) (os : List COp) : CState :=
  (crun k (CState.init statics) os).getD (CState.init statics)

end Exec

/-- Combined library states reachable from `CState.init statics` (§47) by `ok` steps of the kernel
and of the three libraries (Part XIV; HandlePool v0.4 annex; DS-v1). -/
inductive CReach (k : K) (statics : Statics) : CState → Prop where
  | init : CReach k statics (CState.init statics)
  | step {C C' : CState} {o : COp} : CReach k statics C → CRel k C o (.ok C') →
      CReach k statics C'

section Runs
variable (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable]
  [DecidablePred k.Pinned] [DecidablePred k.ExternalDone] [DecidablePred k.Deallocable]
  [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)] [∀ p ls s, Decidable (k.Satisfiable p ls s)]

/-- A run of `os` from `CState.init statics` (§47) has only `ok` steps and reaches `C`; `C` is
library-reachable, and its kernel state is reached by kernel steps O1–O16 and ends of slot contents
(§57; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3). -/
structure CRunsTo (statics : Statics) (os : List COp) (C : CState) : Prop where
  /-- Every step is `ok` and the run ends in `C`. -/
  run : crun k (CState.init statics) os = some C
  /-- `C` is library-reachable. -/
  creach : CReach k statics C
  /-- The kernel state of `C` is reached by kernel steps and ends of slot contents. -/
  xreach : HandlePool.XReach k statics C.kern

/-- The run of `os` from `CState.init statics` has only `ok` steps (§47, §57). -/
abbrev CRuns (statics : Statics) (os : List COp) : Prop :=
  CRunsTo k statics os (cfinal k statics os)

end Runs

/-! ## Step soundness (§58) -/

/-- A computed outcome of a projected relation is an outcome of its lift (§58). -/
theorem liftR_liftO {σ : Type} {R : Outcome3 σ → Prop} {emb : σ → CState} {o : Outcome3 σ}
    (h : R o) : LiftR R emb (liftO emb o) := by
  cases o with
  | ok x => exact ⟨x, h, rfl⟩
  | reject => exact h
  | fail => exact h

/-- An outcome of a guarded projected step read on combined outcomes (§58). -/
theorem liftR_guarded {σ : Type} {p : Prop} [Decidable p] {x : σ} {emb : σ → CState} :
    LiftR (Guarded p x) emb (if p then .ok (emb x) else .reject) := by
  split
  · next h => exact ⟨x, .ok h, rfl⟩
  · next h => exact .reject h

/-- `firstFree` finds a free slot at its index (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3). -/
theorem firstFree_some : ∀ {l : List HandlePool.Slot} {i : Nat} {sl : HandlePool.Slot},
    firstFree l = some (i, sl) → l[i]? = some sl ∧ sl.live = false
  | [], _, _, h => by simp [firstFree] at h
  | x :: l, i, sl, h => by
    unfold firstFree at h
    split at h
    · cases e : firstFree l with
      | none => rw [e] at h; cases h
      | some p =>
        rw [e] at h
        simp only [Option.map_some, Option.some.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
        obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := h
        simpa using firstFree_some e
    · next hx =>
      simp only [Option.some.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
      obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := h
      exact ⟨rfl, by simpa using hx⟩

/-- When `firstFree` finds nothing, every slot is live (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3). -/
theorem firstFree_none : ∀ {l : List HandlePool.Slot}, firstFree l = none →
    ∀ sl ∈ l, sl.live = true
  | [], _, _, h => by cases h
  | x :: l, h, sl, hm => by
    unfold firstFree at h
    split at h
    · next hx =>
      cases e : firstFree l with
      | none =>
        rcases List.mem_cons.1 hm with rfl | hm
        · exact hx
        · exact firstFree_none e sl hm
      | some p => rw [e] at h; cases h
    · cases h

/-- A computed `writer` writes its destination (§67). -/
theorem writer_sound {s : S3} {dst a : Nat} (h : writer s dst = some a) :
    Write3Pre s a [dst] := by
  have := List.find?_some h
  simpa using this

section Sound
variable {k : K} [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable]
  [DecidablePred k.Pinned] [DecidablePred k.ExternalDone] [DecidablePred k.Deallocable]
  [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)] [∀ p ls s, Decidable (k.Satisfiable p ls s)]

/-- `allocSlotOut` is an outcome of `AllocSlotStep` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §58). -/
theorem allocSlotOut_sound (P : HandlePool.PState) (j dst : Nat) :
    HandlePool.AllocSlotStep j dst P (allocSlotOut P j dst) := by
  unfold allocSlotOut
  split
  · next hj => exact .noPool hj
  · next pl hj =>
    split
    · next hs =>
      split
